request.spec:
A plan on a sheet may name one of the sheet's descendants (a sheet id on the plan form; PLAN_ADDED
gains sheet=<id> at its end; a sheet that is not a descendant is refused). Its claims are then
generated for the person of the same name on that sheet (none when there is no such person), by
that sheet's rules and written in that sheet's audit; the plan still counts what it made.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A plan on a sheet may name one of the sheet's descendants (a sheet id on the plan form; PLAN_ADDED
gains sheet=<id> at its end; a sheet that is not a descendant is refused). Its claims are then
generated for the person of the same name on that sheet (none when there is no such person), by
that sheet's rules and written in that sheet's audit; the plan still counts what it made.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A plan can now name one of its sheet's descendants, and its claims are generated on that sheet. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec. After that run I only edited comments in two endpoint YAML files, so I didn't run it again.

**What changed**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V101__plan_sheet.sql`, adds a nullable `target_sheet` column to `plan`. It's empty when the plan works on its own sheet.
- **Adding a plan:** the request takes an optional `sheet`. `ValidatePlan` turns down any sheet that isn't one of the current sheet's descendants: the server returns a 400, nothing is stored or audited, and the form shows `plan-error`. When a sheet is named, `PLAN_ADDED` ends with `sheet=<id>`; otherwise the line is unchanged.
- **Generating (`GeneratePlans`):** for a plan that names a sheet:
  - it looks up the person of the same name on that sheet and skips the plan if there isn't one;
  - claims go through that sheet's rules and are written to that sheet's audit, including `CLAIM_ADDED`, `LATE_ENTRY` and `ROLLUP`;
  - the plan still counts what it made.
- **Front end:** the plan form has a new `plan-form-sheet` field, and a plan's row shows "on sheet …" when it names one.

**Behaviour you might not expect**
- **Which today applies:** plan dates still run up to the *plan's own sheet's* today, not the descendant's. That's what the test requires: the child sheet stays on 2026-03-01 while it gets claims dated 03-06 and 03-11.
- **Name lookup includes aliases:** I reused the existing `findByName`, which also matches aliases (case ignored), so an alias on the descendant sheet counts as the same name.
- **Plan with no matching person:** the plan makes no claims, but its next dates still move forward with its own sheet's today.
